C4-R1.why these cuts: 1.0 is the gate's own bar on a held-out mean. 2.0 is past both CAL residuals the knee trades (Mixtral-8x7B +1.25 on A2, +1.49 on C2's board; Qwen2-57B -1.44) and near Phi-3.5's 128g1 stake (-2.32 against v5''): a reading past it is larger than any residual the four models leave

C4-R2.what: Lambda = sum(counted - W2) / sum(M4 - W2) over C4-B's NATIVE cells' w1 dram_bytes_read: 0 when the counters are W2's, 1 when they are M4's. The W2 lever (sum(M4 - W2) / sum(M4)) is beside. Phi-3.5's bytes lever, held out for the first time
C4-R2.method: counted reads by kneefit.cells_of (refit4 r4.counter_cells: NATIVE, BLOCK_M 128); W2's and M4's reads by r6.reads_of(cell, 6.0, 'W2') and r6.reads_of(cell, 6.0, None) on the same counts and shuffle seed; the same quantities on w2 beside (DESCRIPTIVE)
C4-R2.validity: NOT READ unless the board reads valid, the page is the registered tile and file (read_c2.check_counter_page), the census reads 2 CTAs per SM with verdict COMPLETE, at least 4 NATIVE cells are priced under both laws, and the W2 lever is at least 0.03 (at registration, on the page's six cells: 14.66% on the sum-based measure the cut tests, 15.09% per-cell median)

means.W2-SIDE: W2 prices tp2's w1 bytes at P 112: same-wave w1 re-reads about 0.4 of a wave apart are served, as the law says. Phi-3.5's bytes lever (W2's w1 bytes 9% under M4's, ROUND3.md section 4) passes its first held-out test
means.BETWEEN: the counted w1 bytes sit between W2's and M4's: the law serves too many of the re-reads it moves. Phi-3.5's bytes lever is partly the law's error; the declared round may not keep W2's w1 service as it is
means.M4-SIDE: the re-reads W2 serves at P 112 miss, as M4 prices them: W2's w1 service at P near 100 is the law's error, and Phi-3.5's w1 bytes under W2 are suspect. The declared round keeps M4's w1 at this distance (ROUND3.md section 3's 'W2 on w2 only' row moves the four-model table by 0.2 points or less)
means.BEYOND-W2: fewer w1 bytes than even W2 prices: more re-reads are served than the launch law places under the cut. W2's direction holds at P 112; its size does not
means.BEYOND-M4: more w1 bytes than M4 prices: neither law describes w1 at P 112; the declared round has no measured w1 law at Phi-3.5's distance
means.NOT READ: no held-out test of the w1 bytes lever: Phi-3.5's lever stays untested

C4-R2.why these cuts: thirds of the distance between the two laws: a reading is W2's or M4's when the counters sit within a third of it from that law, so the lever (14.66% at registration, against the byte-page noise B2 assumes, 1.75% x s) is resolved three ways

C4-S1.what: tp2's x (bytes-only / floor-only) per GEMM on its kept cells, with M4's bytes and with W2's

C4-S2.what: tp2 b128g1: K1 at its SEEN constants on counted bytes per GEMM in the wall domain (knee4.py's target and kappa_row) and in the cycles domain beside, and the per-cell w1 + w2 sum: does the knee carry X?

C4-S3.what: tp2's own sag on its b128g1 page: C4's par estimator minus the measured off, us; its own fit

C4-S5.what: the board: C4's per-page (A, tau) beside A2's and C2's, the power read-back, the lock probe, G-BAND; tp2's compiled CTAs per SM at 128x128 beside the 2 per SM the frozen pricing uses; calibrate's triad beside A2's 3726.2 GB/s (15 rentals 3725.6 to 3727.6)

after: OWNER DECISIONS 2026-10-27 (registered): C4, then ONE final declared model round (gate: G1 every held-out 128 G 1 mean within 1.0%, Mixtral-8x7B on C2's board as well; G2 estimated P(A) >= 0.5 on the registered cells). If that round fails the B3 gate, iteration stops and the owner chooses between narrowing scope and going blind. B3 is registered only after a declared round passes. If C4 reads NOT READ, the final round runs on the four existing CAL models without tp2, and C4 is not rented again (owner, 2026-10-27). The round-4 gate is unchanged for that final round; G1 covers the five CAL models when C4 is read, the four otherwise
